description: THE HEADLINE MULTI-BODY GOLDEN (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-1 / §Decisions-3): the first user-visible boolean between two INDEPENDENTLY-BUILT bodies. Five features: (1) a 20x20 mm square on the XY origin datum at x,y in [0,20]; (2) extrude add 20 mm up -> body A, a 20x20x20 cube (merge absent -> reads True, creates the first body); (3) a second 20x20 mm square on the SAME XY datum at x in [10,30] (overlapping A in x[10,20]); (4) extrude add 20 mm up with merge=FALSE -> body B, a SECOND 20x20x20 cube NOT fused into A (the part now holds bodies={A, B}, overlapping but distinct — MB-0's second-body seam); (5) a `boolean` feature, operation `union`, target=extrude A / tool=extrude B. The union fuses the two overlapping cubes into ONE connected solid: the result takes over the target's identity slot and the tool body is removed, so the part ends with a SINGLE body. Because A covers x[0,20] and B covers x[10,30] with identical y,z in [0,20], their union is EXACTLY a 30x20x20 box (they together tile x[0,30] with full y,z; clean() merges the coplanar face splits at the former x=10/x=20 seams into a perfect box). Locks the MB-1a union path end to end: (a) two-body resolution by base-feature id against EvaluationState.bodies; (b) OCCT fuse (BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse) + clean(); (c) the single-connected-solid-per-body invariant (shells=1); (d) operand replacement (target survives, tool consumed); and -- via the parametrized gates -- byte-identical GLB across an interpreter restart + STEP round-trip re-measure.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Body A: a 20x20 square, corners (0,0)-(20,20) mm on the XY datum (normal +Z at z=0), extrude add 20 mm up -> cube A spanning x,y in [0,20], z in [0,20]. Body B: a 20x20 square at corners (10,0)-(30,20) mm on the same XY datum, extrude add 20 mm up (merge=false) -> cube B spanning x in [10,30], y in [0,20], z in [0,20]. The cubes OVERLAP in the block x[10,20] x y[0,20] x z[0,20] (a 10x20x20 = 4000 mm^3 region). union(A,B) merges them into one solid.

volume = |A| + |B| - |A intersect B| = 8000 + 8000 - (10*20*20 = 4000) = 12000 mm^3 exactly (inclusion-exclusion; the overlap block is counted once, not twice). Equivalently the union IS a 30x20x20 box = 30*20*20 = 12000. Measured deviation vs analytic: 0.0 (an exact prism fuse of axis-aligned boxes).

surface_area = the union is a 30x20x20 rectangular box, so area = 2*(30*20 + 30*20 + 20*20) = 2*(600 + 600 + 400) = 2*1600 = 3200 mm^2. Every internal face (A's and B's mutual boundary in the overlap) is consumed by the fuse; no seam face survives. Measured deviation: 0.0.

centroid = (15, 10, 10) mm: the centroid of the 30x20x20 box spanning x[0,30], y[0,20], z[0,20] is its geometric center (15, 10, 10). (Cross-check by inclusion-exclusion over the mass: (8000*(10,10,10) + 8000*(20,10,10) - 4000*(15,10,10)) / 12000 = ((80000+160000-60000)/12000, 10, 10) = (180000/12000, 10, 10) = (15, 10, 10).) Measured deviation: 0.0 on all three components.
bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[30,20,20]: the union spans x from A's min 0 to B's max 30, y[0,20], z[0,20]. An exact prism fuse of axis-aligned boxes, so all six bounds are EXACT (measured deviation 0.0).

topology = 6 faces, 12 edges, 1 SHELL: the union is a single connected box. shells=1 is the load-bearing MB-1 assertion -- the two overlapping lumps fuse into ONE connected solid (the single-connected-solid-per-body invariant, §Decisions-3), unlike the disjoint golden's shells=2. clean() (ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain) merges the coplanar face fragments the fuse leaves at the former x=10 and x=20 seams, so the box reduces to its canonical 6 faces / 12 edges. Euler-Poincare cross-check: V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 2 = 2*(1-0), a valid closed genus-0 manifold solid.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, faceted per-face normals, no vertex sharing across faces -- the box-golden convention): each of the 6 planar quad faces -> 4 vertices / 2 triangles; 6 faces = 24 vertices / 12 triangles.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The union of two axis-aligned overlapping prisms (Solid.extrude bodies fused via OCCT BRepAlgoAPI_Fuse + ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain clean) is geometrically an exact 30x20x20 box. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-18, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume, surface_area, centroid (x/y/z), and all six bounding-box bounds are EXACTLY 0.0 -- the fuse of coincident axis-aligned faces introduces no numerical error at this scale. Documented ceiling 1e-9 (matching the sibling multibody-two-disjoint-boxes golden) is pure headroom over the observed 0.0 worst case, for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). The solver contributes zero error by construction (both squares are shape-pinned, under-constrained only in whole-sketch position -> planegcs returns the drawn positions bitwise; solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
